title: BPP cursor_recover result (DESIGN.md §14.4, §15.3; registry R41 originating)
description: Success.result for cursor_recover (gap notes G4/G40): §14.4's 'typed problem plus authorized snapshot recovery options' encoded as recovery_mode — resume returns a fresh audience-bound token continuing without loss; snapshot_restart names the authorized snapshot to re-read before continuing from snapshot_continuation (after retention lapse or an incarnation/recovery-epoch fence, §15.3).

continuation.description: Fresh audience-bound token; present exactly when recovery_mode is resume — gap note G40.

snapshot_continuation.description: Token continuing strictly after the named snapshot; present exactly when recovery_mode is snapshot_restart — gap note G40.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3).

class.description: Digest class per the §14.2 table; substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_id.description: Key id for keyed classes (raw HMAC keys and per-object salts are never part of a DigestRef).

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef (§14.2): every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash.

continuationToken.description: Opaque scope- and audience-bound continuation token (§14.4): it carries an authenticated cursor, endpoint incarnation, recovery epoch, filter digest, and retention semantics and is never parsed or constructed by the caller; 4096-byte visible-ASCII bound — gap note G38.
